source_facts.fact: Current GOV.UK guidance states that, subject to exceptions, mandatory BNG in England requires at least a 10% increase in biodiversity value measured using the statutory biodiversity metric.
source_facts.gate: A generic 10% rule cannot be turned into a parcel biodiversity-unit requirement without a site baseline and applicable exemption check.

source_facts.fact: GOV.UK says that from 6 August 2026 BNG will not apply to planning applications for developments with a red-line site area of 0.2 hectares or below, subject to priority-habitat caveats and other rules.
source_facts.gate: On 25 July 2026 this future-effective rule is not yet in force and must not be backdated.

source_facts.fact: BNG becomes mandatory for nationally significant infrastructure projects from 2 November 2026.
source_facts.gate: The future NSIP start date must not be represented as current July 2026 law in force.

source_facts.fact: The responsible-authority page was updated 26 June 2026 and records publication progress across England, including Greater London published in March 2026.
source_facts.gate: An LNRS priority or opportunity area is not itself planning permission, land allocation or a parcel biodiversity score.

source_facts.fact: Natural England guidance updated 11 March 2026 covers 27 nutrient-neutrality catchments and records River Camel and River Eden boundary-related calculator changes.
source_facts.gate: A catchment calculator output requires site-specific inputs and cannot be inferred from catchment membership alone.

source_facts.fact: Planning Data publishes current datasets for ancient woodland, SSSI, SAC and SPA with explicit origin/quality metadata.
source_facts.gate: Dataset intersection is screening evidence and does not replace authoritative designation documents, field survey, HRA or planning decision.

core_rules: the generic 10 percent BNG objective does not calculate biodiversity units for a parcel
BNG applicability must be checked before applying the statutory metric
the 0.2 hectare exemption effective 6 August 2026 must not be backdated to July 2026
future NSIP BNG rules effective 2 November 2026 must not be represented as currently in force
householder and other statutory exemptions must be checked before requiring BNG
priority habitat caveats can prevent use of certain exemptions and must not be ignored
de minimis thresholds require actual on-site habitat-impact evidence
a red-line boundary area is not the same as habitat area affected
biodiversity units require habitat type condition size and other metric inputs
metric output is not valid without a site-specific baseline
an ecologist assessment cannot be replaced by a national dataset intersection
on-site BNG is not automatically achievable because land exists within the red line
off-site biodiversity units are not assumed available without registered and secured gains
statutory biodiversity credits are a last-resort route and not an assumed project cost
BNG legal agreements and habitat-management periods must not be inferred from planning policy alone
a biodiversity gain plan is not approved merely because planning permission exists
planning permission subject to the biodiversity gain condition is not the same as discharge of that condition
BNG applies to habitats within the red-line boundary according to current statutory rules and exemptions
irreplaceable habitat has separate treatment and must not be offset as ordinary habitat
ancient woodland is irreplaceable habitat and requires specific planning consideration
ancient woodland inventory intersection is screening evidence not a field-verified boundary survey
ancient woodland dataset completeness and update dates must be retained
ASNW and PAWS statuses must remain distinct when available
an LNRS priority is not a statutory planning allocation
an LNRS opportunity area is not planning permission
LNRS publication status must be date-versioned by responsible authority
a draft or unpublished LNRS must not be represented as a published strategy
Greater London LNRS publication does not make every mapped opportunity a development constraint or permission
nutrient-neutrality requirements apply only where the relevant protected-site/catchment advice and project type trigger them
membership of a nutrient catchment does not itself calculate a nutrient budget
nutrient calculators require project wastewater land-use and mitigation inputs
March 2026 calculator boundary changes must not be applied to earlier historical states without versioning
wastewater treatment upgrades must not be assumed complete because they are represented in a future calculator scenario
nutrient mitigation availability must not be fabricated
nutrient credits or mitigation schemes are not planning permission
a zero or negative calculated nutrient budget cannot be inferred without running the applicable calculator
HRA screening is not the same as Appropriate Assessment
a likely significant effect finding is not an automatic final refusal
absence of a mapped SAC or SPA intersection does not prove absence of HRA pathways
SAC SPA and Ramsar designations must remain distinct
SSSI designation is not identical to European-site designation
SSSI condition category is not a parcel development score
favourable SSSI condition does not remove statutory consultation duties where triggered
unfavourable SSSI condition does not automatically make every nearby project unacceptable
SSSI activities can require Natural England consent or assent depending on actor and activity
SSSI advice processes are not planning permission
a Section 28i advice request is not an assent decision
Natural England response times must not be interpreted as permission unless the governing process explicitly says so
protected-site boundaries can change and designation updates must be date-versioned
Planning Data SSSI origin warnings must be preserved
Planning Data SAC origin warnings must be preserved
Planning Data SPA origin warnings must be preserved
Planning Data dataset counts are service-level metadata and not evidence about a specific parcel
Planning Data collector date is not the legal designation date
a spatial overlap from beta Planning Data must be verified against authoritative designation evidence before promotion
protected-site proximity alone is not an HRA conclusion
impact pathways can extend beyond a designation boundary
EIA screening and scoping are procedural stages not permission outcomes
Schedule 1 and Schedule 2 EIA treatment must not be inferred without project type and threshold checks
an Environmental Statement is not evidence that environmental effects are acceptable
mitigation proposed in an EIA is not delivered mitigation until secured and implemented
HRA derogation stages must not be assumed reachable without prior tests
public-interest arguments do not bypass HRA legal tests
Natural England standing advice is a material planning consideration not a parcel score
protected-species licensing is separate from planning permission
ecological survey age season and method can affect validity and must not be inferred from national data
NO_DATA on ecology remains unknown rather than no-constraint
national environmental evidence must not be converted directly into land value or Future Growth score
